transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-24
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jules Ortega (Redwood SE), Oliver Park (CTO, Stormhaven), Lena Rossi (Head of Infra), Kayla Nguyen (Security Eng)
Shared links: Redwood security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2.pdf), SAML config guide (https://redwood.example.com/docs/saml-okta), Dedicated pilot template (link sent in chat)

[00:00] Maya: Hi all, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off — I'm Maya, I'm the AE, and with me is Jules from our infra team. Quick sound check?
[00:12] Oliver: Sounds good, yeah, Oliver here. Thanks for making time.
[00:15] Lena: Lena on my end.
[00:18] Kayla: Kayla, hi.
[00:20] Jules: Hey folks. Quick agenda — security posture, hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), KMS/encryption, SSO and RBAC, logs/retention, then next steps. Anything to add?
[00:32] Oliver: No, that covers it. We — mainly want to make sure we can run inference on customer data without exposing PII and meet our auditors.

[00:37] Maya: Great. High level first — Stormhaven, can you share current infra and compliance baseline? Are you SOC2 or ISO scoped today?
[00:44] Oliver: We're SOC2 type 2 in scope, working toward ISO27001 by Q2 next year. We have Okta for SSO, and we use AWS KMS with a mixture of AWS-managed keys and our own BYOK for some regulated workloads.
[00:58] Kayla: Yeah we enforce RBAC via Okta groups tied into our internal IAM; audit retention is currently 1 year for syslogs, but application-level logs are 90 days. We also have data residency requirements for EU customer subsets.

[01:15] Maya: Sounds aligned — Redwood's hosted API offers quick onboarding but for sensitive workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools with customer tenancy and optional BYOK; Private gives a private control plane and can be on VPC or on-prem.
[01:33] Lena: Can you explain the BYOK flow? We need HSM-backed keys and hold control, not hand over keys.
[01:40] Jules: Sure — we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. For AWS KMS you can grant a key policy that allows Redwood service principal to decrypt for inference runtime. We also have an HSM-backed BYOK path for Private deployments where the keys never leave your vault. There's a little config plumbing for Dedicated where you mount a key alias and we reference it in runtime — it's not typical to export the key.
[02:05] Kayla: Ok, so for Hosted — would we need to grant Redwood cross-account decrypt? We're cautious about that.
[02:12] Maya: For Hosted there's an option to use Redwood-managed keys or you can do a restricted KMS role. However if you need full key custody, Hosted might not fit; Dedicated with BYOK or Private is better.
[02:25] Oliver: Right, cost is also a factor. We like the idea of hosted for early dev but need to know when to move to Dedicated.

[02:35] Jules: From a perf/cost tradeoff: Hosted is easiest, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and SLA, Private gives maximum control but higher ops overhead. We can set autoscale and burst policies for Dedicated to match your throughput spikes — that reduces per-token cost if steady usage.
[02:53] Lena: How about audit logs? We need immutable audit trails for all inference requests and admin actions. Retention 1 year preferred, with export to our SIEM.
[03:03] Maya: Redwood Console emits audit logs and admin events; logs can be streamed to your S3 or to a SIEM via webhook or syslog forwarder. Retention defaults are 90 days on Hosted but can be extended as an add-on; Dedicated allows configurable retention and direct forwarding.
[03:20] Kayla: Are logs tamper-evident? We have auditors asking about integrity guarantees.
[03:24] Jules: Good question — we append checksums and maintain sequence numbering; for Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your WORM storage or ship to an append-only log service. We'll include the technical writeup in the pack.

[03:40] Oliver: About SSO — we use Okta, SCIM provisioning, and need SAML-based SSO and group mapping into RBAC. Is that supported?
[03:48] Maya: Yes — SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning is supported. You'll be able to map Okta groups to Redwood roles (Admin/Dev/Observer). We also support fine-grained API key permissions, token scoping, and short-lived tokens for programmatic access.
[04:04] Kayla: For programmatic calls from our backend, we prefer not to store long-lived API keys. Short lived with KMS-backed signing is ideal.
[04:11] Jules: We have token rotation and recommended patterns for ephemeral credentials. For Dedicated/Private you can also use mTLS and internal auth hooks.

[04:27] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[04:29] Lena: Can you walk through a typical onboarding for Dedicated? Timeline?
[04:33] Maya: Sure; discovery (this call), security review and SOC/ISO docs, pilot with sample traffic (2 weeks typical), then procurement/contracting and capacity reservation. Onboarding for Dedicated is usually 4-6 weeks from pilot sign-off.
[04:48] Oliver: For pilot we need baseline perf numbers — 99th percentile latency under 150ms for our 512 token typical prompt. Can you commit that?
[04:58] Jules: We'll run a targeted perf run on similarly provisioned hardware; we can't guarantee without benchmarking your prompt shapes, but historically for the model families you mentioned we see 95-140ms p99 under moderate concurrency on Dedicated. We'll include an explicit benchmark run as part of the pilot.

[05:15] Kayla: On data retention — inference inputs vs outputs: do you store prompts by default on Hosted?
[05:22] Maya: Hosted logs request metadata by default and you can opt into full request/response logging for debugging. For customers who need zero retention we provide redact-at-ingest and opt-out pathways; Dedicated/Private can be configured to never persist payloads or to only keep ephemeral caches. We'll note that in the security pack.
[05:40] Oliver: How granular is RBAC? We want to ensure junior devs can't access PII in prompts, but can still run non-PII tests.
[05:48] Jules: Roles can be scoped per-project and per-model route. We also support route-level permissions and token-level ACLs; combined with SCIM group mapping you can enforce least-privilege. For deeper separation, Private deployment can run in tenant VPCs so the admin plane is under your control.

[06:05] Lena: Any concerns about model debugging features leaking keys or data into logs?
[06:10] Maya: Debugging traces are opt-in and stored separately; we can configure them to go to your S3 or not persist. Also function/tool calls are scrubbed by default unless you enable verbose traces.

[06:26] Kayla: About compliance evidence — can you share SOC2 Type II report and pen test summaries?
[06:30] Maya: Absolutely — attaching the SOC2 PDF and a high-level pen test summary to the deal. See the link in chat. Also ISO scope summary forthcoming.
[06:40] Oliver: Thanks. Any network-level controls? VPC peering, private endpoints?
[06:45] Jules: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering or private egress options; Private can run entirely in your VPC with customer-managed control plane. We also support restricting egress to your IP allowlist and mutual TLS.

[07:00] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[07:02] Lena: Can we get SIEM integration — forwarding logs to Splunk?
[07:06] Maya: Yes — Splunk/Sumo/Datadog integrations supported via streaming. We'll provide syslog/HTTP ingest configs.

[07:18] Kayla: Encryption at rest details? AES-256? Are tokens encrypted in transit end-to-end?
[07:23] Jules: We use TLS1.2+ for in-transit; for at-rest we use AES-256-GCM. Keys can be managed by Redwood or by your KMS. For BYOK we don't store key material in plaintext; we reference key IDs/aliases.

[07:38] Oliver: One blocker — auditors require an independent key separation between data plane and control plane. Does Redwood separate those duties?
[07:46] Maya: Yes, we have separation of control and data plane responsibilities. For Dedicated we can deploy the control plane in a tenant-specific instance and ensure operators don't have access to cryptographic key material when BYOK is used. We'll include the architecture diagram in the pack.

[08:02] Lena: Licensing/pricing question — what is the delta to move from Hosted to Dedicated in terms of minimum commit?
[08:08] Maya: Dedicated has a monthly minimum based on reserved GPU capacity; we typically see customers commit 3-6 months initially. Exact numbers depend on the model family and required throughput — we'll produce a sample pricing sheet for your expected qps.

[08:25] Kayla: SLAs — availability and latency SLOs?
[08:29] Jules: For Dedicated we provide SLA-backed uptime (99.9% typical) and latency SLOs configurable per-route. Hosted has best-effort latency targets but not the same contractual guarantees.

[08:44] Oliver: About data residency — can Dedicated instances be placed in eu-west-1 only?
[08:49] Maya: Yes, region locking is supported. For Private the control plane can be hosted in regional zones or on-prem if required.

[09:00] Lena: We also need long-term retention for audit logs (3+ years) immutability. Is that supported?
[09:06] Jules: We can export logs daily to your S3 with lifecycle policies and WORM settings to meet 3-year retention. There may be additional cost for long-term storage.

[09:18] Kayla: Do you support customer-managed SIEM keys for signing logs?
[09:22] Jules: We can sign log batches with your KMS key if integrated in the pipeline — that's part of Dedicated/Private flows.

[09:32] Oliver: Anything else we should know about access governance?
[09:35] Maya: We recommend combining SCIM-based group sync with short-lived tokens and route-level ACLs. For high-assurance roles we support MFA enforced via Okta policies.

[09:50] Lena: Are there known limitations with specific open models you host? Quantized models or kv cache issues?
[09:57] Jules: Some older quantized variants can have slightly different perf characteristics; our runtime manages KV cache and it's optimized for common attention patterns, but we'll run your prompt set in the pilot to validate.

[10:12] Kayla: Regarding legal — we have specific contracting requests around data processing addendum and export controls.
[10:18] Maya: We have standard DPA templates and can add export controls clauses; procurement will coordinate during the legal phase.

[10:28] (brief pause)
[10:30] Oliver: Let's talk timeline — if we get SOC2 and perf benchmarks, we can greenlight a pilot in early Oct? Procurement aside.
[10:37] Maya: Sounds reasonable; we'll target pilot start 2026-10-05. I'll confirm in the follow-up email.

[10:44] Kayla: One last nit: can you show us the exact RBAC roles and a mapping example?
[10:48] Jules: Yes — I'll send a sample mapping (Okta group -> Redwood role) and a demo clip showing SCIM provisioning.

[10:56] Maya: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Attach SOC2/ISO docs, SAML/SCIM guide, perf runbook, draft Dedicated pilot plan and pricing. Kayla will send retention and PII scope.
[11:12] Oliver: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[11:14] Lena: Thanks, bye.
[11:15] Kayla: Bye.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: some words run together, occasional mislabeling (Speaker 3 appears once); action items captured above.
